To begin with, I’d like to pick up *#659 (unit tests for `types/state.go`)*: <https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/issues/659|github.com/datazip-inc/olake/issues/659>

Could someone let me know the process for getting this issue assigned to me?
Happy to pick up more issues and contribute further after this one. :rocket:

attachments.text:
**Problem*

The OLake codebase currently has unit tests for:
• `resolver`
• `flattener`
• `catalog`
However, the file `olake/types/state.go` does not have any test coverage.
This file handles critical state management logic for the OLake connector, including:
• *State Management Methods:*  
   • `SetType()` - Sets the state type (GLOBAL, STREAM, MIXED)  
   • `ResetStreams()` - Resets all stream states  
   • `ResetCursor()` - Resets cursor values for a specific stream  
   • `isZero()` - Checks if state is empty
• *Global State Operations:*  
   • `GetGlobal()` - Retrieves global state with read lock  
   • `SetGlobal()` - Sets or updates global state with stream tracking  
   • `HasCompletedBackfill()` - Checks if backfill is completed for a stream (supports both GLOBAL and STREAM state types)
• *Cursor Management:*  
   • `GetCursor()` - Retrieves cursor value for a stream and key  
   • `SetCursor()` - Sets cursor value for a stream (creates new StreamState if needed)
• *Chunk Management:*  
   • `GetChunks()` - Retrieves all chunks for a stream  
   • `SetChunks()` - Sets chunks for a stream (skips for FULLREFRESH mode)  
   • `RemoveChunk()` - Removes a specific chunk and returns remaining count
etc.
Without unit tests, bugs in state management, race conditions with concurrent access, incorrect serialization/deserialization, or edge cases with nil values, empty states, or chunk operations may slip through during development. This is particularly critical as the `State` struct is used extensively across the codebase including:
• Incremental sync operations
• Backfill operations
• CDC (Change Data Capture) processing etc.

---

**Proposed Solution*

Add comprehensive unit tests for the logic inside `state.go`.
This will help:
• Increase overall test coverage
• Improve state management reliability across different state types
• Catch bugs earlier during CI, especially around:  
   • Concurrent access patterns (read/write locks)  
   • State serialization/deserialization edge cases  
   • Chunk management operations  
   • Cursor value handling  
   • Empty state handling
• Make contributions safer when modifying state management logic
For reference on how existing unit tests are structured, you can refer to *PR #273* and the existing `catalog_test.go`, `flatten_test.go` and `resolver_test.go` files.

---

**Notes for Contributors*

• Add tests covering most of the scenarios and edge cases which should indicate both pass and fail scenarios.
• Follow the existing test file structure and naming conventions to maintain consistency with other parts (see `catalog_test.go` for reference).
• Use `testify/assert` and `testify/require` for assertions (as seen in existing test files).
